record.context_brief: Property (SC) for convex weakly compact sets
record.original_question: Does the family cwk(X) of all nonempty convex weakly compact subsets of a Banach space X have property (SC), meaning that one can choose a selector on cwk(X) whose composition with every scalarly measurable multifunction into cwk(X) is scalarly measurable?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.9 (Fremlin, [59]). Does the family cwk(X) of all convex weakly compact non-empty subsets of X have property (SC)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $\mathrm{cwk}(X)$ denote the family of all nonempty convex weakly compact subsets of $X$. Given a complete probability space $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$, a multifunction $F\colon\Omega\to\mathrm{cwk}(X)$ is said to be scalarly measurable if for every $x^*\in X^*$ the real-valued support function $\omega\mapsto s(x^*,F(\omega))=\sup\{x^*(x):x\in F(\omega)\}$ is $\Sigma$-measurable. A function $f\colon\Omega\to X$ is called a scalarly measurable selector of $F$ if $f(\omega)\in F(\omega)$ for every $\omega\in\Omega$ and $x^*\circ f$ is measurable for every $x^*\in X^*$.

The family $\mathrm{cwk}(X)$ is said to have property (SC) if there exists a map $\sigma\colon\mathrm{cwk}(X)\to X$ with $\sigma(C)\in C$ for all $C\in\mathrm{cwk}(X)$ such that for every complete probability space $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$ and every scalarly measurable multifunction $F\colon\Omega\to\mathrm{cwk}(X)$, the composition $\sigma\circ F\colon\Omega\to X$ is a scalarly measurable selector of $F$.

Determine whether, for every Banach space $X$, the family $\mathrm{cwk}(X)$ has property (SC).
artifact.status_search_result: The question, attributed to Fremlin, is listed as an open problem in surveys on measurability and selections of multifunctions in Banach spaces. No published resolution was found; partial positive results exist for restricted classes (e.g., specific Banach spaces or weakly compactly generated cases), but the general problem appears to remain open.
